messages:
Maya Patel: quick sync — i'm thinking about breaking the monolithic routing policy into 3 independently deployable phases: match -> score -> enforcement. pros are safer rollouts and smaller hotpaths. cons? more cross-service chatter. thoughts?
Ravi Singh: +1 on safer rollouts. what's the signal surface between match and score? if it's heavy, we'll blow up p99.
Maya Patel: proposal: match returns a small set of candidate route ids + cheap attributes (region, tier, compatibility flags). scoring pulls telemetry and cost hints to compute final score. all IDs are stable across versions.
Liam O'Connor: stable ids help. but how do we handle tenant overrides (eg custom pref for region)? We can't call tenant db from every request.
Evelyn Park: cache tenant overrides in the policy sidecar with TTL and cache invalidation on write. cheaper than a sync call.
Andre Gomez: sidecar cache is neat but ops complexity grows. what about embedding a thin override vector in the request at the edge? the edge would read tenant config once per session.
Maya Patel: edge-provided override raises trust/bypass concerns. want to validate and sign override vector — that's doable but adds crypto ops.
Ravi Singh: another angle: compress override into a single bitmask + version. sidecar can validate version quickly. keeps request small.
Liam O'Connor: ok. on scoring: we should keep score computation pure functional (no side effects) to allow in-process evaluation for Dedicated flow. then enforcement can be a separate async writer for auditing.
Evelyn Park: that separation helps: testing invariants on scoring becomes trivial. we can run a canary scorer in sim mode.
Andre Gomez: tradeoff: duplicating logic (in-process for Dedicated vs sidecar for Hosted) might diverge. need strong integration tests.
Maya Patel: agree. testing strategy: property-based tests for scorer (inputs -> monotonicity/cost-latency invariants) + nightly sim against production traces. also require scorer version pinning on rollouts.
Ravi Singh: what about policy language? current JSON blobs are messy. i'd like a compact DSL that compiles to stable opcodes. then we can run different runtimes (wasm, native) from same spec.
Liam O'Connor: wasm runtime for scoring is attractive — sandboxed, hot-reloadable. but cold-start overhead matters. we should cache compiled modules per host.
Evelyn Park: and keep a fallback native scorer if wasm cold start fails. graceful degrade.
Maya Patel: good. make wasm optional path. default path native optimized kernels. wasm used for tenant-supplied extensions or experiments.
Andre Gomez: ops note: we need versioned compatibility matrix. runtime vX supports opcode set Y. old policies must be blocked or auto-translated.
Ravi Singh: about telemetry: scoring should emit deterministic labels to make attribution possible. avoid free-form strings in hot loop. structured enums only.
Liam O'Connor: also add per-route cost_estimate and latency_hint fields output by scorer so the router can do fast admission control without recomputing.
Evelyn Park: eviction and preemption: instead of tight coupling, expose a priority token from scorer. the admission service consumes tokens to accept/reject when under pressure.
Maya Patel: summary action items: (1) draft minimal match->score->enforce API (proto), (2) design stable route id scheme, (3) prototype scorer DSL->wasm compilation, (4) sim harness for nightly trace replay. i'll own API + IDs.
Ravi Singh: i'll take the DSL proposal + property tests.
Liam O'Connor: i'll prototype wasm bootstrap with module cache.
Evelyn Park: i'll mock the sidecar override cache + invalidation flow and test TTLs.
Andre Gomez: i'll write the compatibility matrix template and ops playbook for rollbacks.
ops-bot: Deploybot: created epic "policy-decomposition-staging" in JIRA (RD-7892) and assigned to Maya. :white_check_mark:
Maya Patel: thanks — can we aim to have a first-pass proto by EOD Friday? short-cycle so we discover friction early.
Ravi Singh: sounds good. i'll start a doc with examples and a couple of counterexamples to force edge cases.
Liam O'Connor: ping me on infra slack when you have the wasm build, i'll help with caching layer.
Evelyn Park: adding a note: watch out for metric cardinality explosion if scorer emits tenant-level enums. we'll aggregate at route/region granularity by default.
Maya Patel: good call. last thing — keep fallback semantics explicit in proto: exact and best_effort modes. we don't want silent behavior drift.
Andre Gomez: +1. explicit wins.
Maya Patel: cool — closing for now. will post the proto link in this thread when ready. :v:
